noveltyJustification: All three findings are new to this run: the mixed id/alias bundle defect, the selectionKinds gap and the ROUTER.md projection drift. Weighted new = 5 + 1 + 1 = 7 against weighted total 7, so the ratio is 1.0.
ruledOut: Substring false positives in the routing vocabulary: every keyword checked, no common-word collision
Stale runtime mirror feeding the harness: all seven authored files byte-identical between .opencode and .skilled
Advisor id-noun rule still lifting on a bare noun: lexicalEvidence comes from the skill own candidate haystack
ambiguityDelta absorbing the mixed-form gap: scores are multiples of 4 and the delta is 1

title: Mixed id and alias forms drop a named mode from the bundle
description: scoreModes counts distinct fold-deduped keywords, so a full mcp-* id scores two hits while a short alias scores one; the 4-point gap exceeds ambiguityDelta 1 and selectNearTiedModes drops the second named mode.
scopeProof: Both prompts sit inside the hub routing contract; scorer, vocabulary and outcome promise are all in the declared review target.

title: selectionKinds cannot express the bundle kind the compiler can emit
description: bundleKindForModes can return surfaceBundle while destinationGraph.selectionKinds is hardcoded to single and orderedBundle, so the comment claiming the rule survives a role change overstates it.
scopeProof: Compiler and its selection-kind list are both inside the compiled-routing surface of the declared review target.

title: ROUTER.md calls itself the single machine-readable projection while a second one is live
description: ROUTER.md section 3 calls itself the single machine-readable projection but declares four intent signals while hub-router.json declares three routerSignals; the keyword union matches, the structure does not.
scopeProof: Both files are hub-owned and inside the declared review target.
